values.content: You are a conservative visual analyst. Describe only visible thumbnail evidence. Do not infer views, click-through rate, audience response, or creator intent. Return the required JSON schema.

nodes.name: Aggregate Competitor Evidence
nodes.notes: Combines successful analyses, keeps failures visible, and labels the evidence state as complete, partial, or failed.

parameters.jsCode:
const rows = $input.all().map((item) => item.json);
const brief = $('Set Template Configuration').first().json;
const usable = rows.filter((row) => row.analysis_ok);
const analysisStatus = usable.length === rows.length ? 'complete' : usable.length > 0 ? 'partial' : 'failed';

const evidence = usable.map((row) => ({
  video_id: row.video_id,
  source_url: row.source_url,
  source_title: row.source_title,
  author_name: row.author_name,
  thumbnail_url: row.thumbnail_url,
  analysis: row.analysis,
}));

const conceptPrompt = [
  'Create exactly three original YouTube thumbnail concepts for the planned video below.',
  'Use only the supplied competitor analyses as design evidence.',
  'Do not copy a competitor composition, wording, branding, face, artwork, or other protected expression.',
  'Do not claim or predict CTR. Treat the analysis as creative evidence, not performance proof.',
  '',
  'PLANNED VIDEO:',
  JSON.stringify({
    title: brief.planned_video_title,
    promise: brief.video_promise,
    audience: brief.audience,
    target_keyword: brief.target_keyword,
    brand_palette: brief.brand_palette,
    optional_thumbnail_text: brief.thumbnail_text,
    aspect_ratio: brief.aspect_ratio,
  }),
  '',
  'COMPETITOR EVIDENCE:',
  JSON.stringify(evidence),
  '',
  'Each concept must explain which source video IDs informed it, why it is distinct, and which copy risks to avoid.',
  'Prompts must be production-ready for ThumbCanvas, contain one focal point, and request no logos or copied artwork.',
].join('\n');

return [{
  json: {
    planned_video_title: brief.planned_video_title,
    video_promise: brief.video_promise,
    audience: brief.audience,
    target_keyword: brief.target_keyword,
    brand_palette: brief.brand_palette,
    thumbnail_text: brief.thumbnail_text,
    aspect_ratio: brief.aspect_ratio,
    submitted_at: brief.submitted_at,
    workflow_version: brief.workflow_version,
    openai_model: brief.openai_model,
    thumbcanvas_base_url: brief.thumbcanvas_base_url,
    analyses: rows,
    usable_evidence: evidence,
    successful_analysis_count: usable.length,
    analysis_status: analysisStatus,
    has_usable_analysis: usable.length > 0,
    concept_prompt: conceptPrompt,
  },
}];

parameters.content:
## Analyze competitor YouTube thumbnails with OpenAI and save approved briefs to Google Sheets

### Who this is for
YouTube creators, thumbnail designers, and content teams who want evidence-informed creative directions without copying competitors or pretending that visual analysis guarantees click-through rate.

### What it does
This workflow collects a planned-video brief plus two or three public competitor YouTube URLs. It validates and deduplicates the links, retrieves public oEmbed metadata, and sends each public thumbnail to OpenAI for a schema-validated visual analysis. It then aggregates the usable evidence and produces exactly three original thumbnail concepts.

A human review page shows the public sources, the analysis, and all three concepts. Only an approved concept becomes a pre-filled [ThumbCanvas](https://thumbcanvas.com/create-thumbs) link. The approved decision is then appended to Google Sheets as an audit row. Rejected concepts create neither a ThumbCanvas link nor a sheet row.

### Setup
1. Add an OpenAI credential to both OpenAI nodes. The default model is `gpt-4.1-mini`; change it in **Set Template Configuration** if your account uses another vision-capable model.
2. Connect Google Sheets OAuth in **Append Approved Brief to Google Sheets**. Select a spreadsheet and a sheet. Use these header names: `approved_at`, `planned_video_title`, `target_keyword`, `audience`, `competitor_urls`, `approved_concept`, `concept_evidence`, `thumbcanvas_url`, `openai_model`, `analysis_status`, `review_notes`, `workflow_version`.
3. Publish the workflow, open the production form URL, and submit a brief.

### Important boundaries
OpenAI vision can misread small text or visual details, so the workflow exposes sources and limitations for human checking. It never predicts CTR. Enter only public competitor links and non-confidential brief data. OpenAI receives the thumbnail URL and brief context; Google Sheets stores only the approved row. n8n may retain execution data according to your instance settings.

ThumbCanvas generation happens only when the reviewer opens the final link. No image is auto-published.

## 1. Collect and validate

The n8n Form Trigger asks for the planned video, audience, keyword, palette, optional thumbnail text, and two or three public competitor URLs.

**Normalize and Validate Brief** accepts HTTPS YouTube watch, youtu.be, Shorts, and embed links; extracts strict 11-character video IDs; removes duplicates; and rejects packs with fewer than two unique videos. Optional thumbnail text is limited to four words.

Use **Set Template Configuration** to change the OpenAI model or ThumbCanvas base URL in one place. Do not place API keys in fields or Code nodes.

## 2. Gather visible evidence

Each competitor becomes one n8n item. The HTTP Request node reads public YouTube oEmbed metadata; the OpenAI node receives the public thumbnail URL at high image detail and returns a strict visual-analysis schema.

The analysis covers focal subject, visible text, composition, contrast, emotion, hook, transferable patterns, copy risks, confidence, and limitations. It deliberately excludes performance and CTR claims.

Failures continue as labeled items so the aggregate can report `complete`, `partial`, or `failed` evidence instead of silently dropping a source.

## 3. Generate and review

The second OpenAI call receives the planned-video brief and validated visual evidence. Strict structured output requires exactly three original directions, each with source video IDs, rationale, composition, palette, production prompt, and risks.

The workflow then pauses for up to seven days on an n8n Form review page. The reviewer can open the public source videos, compare evidence, approve one concept, add notes, or reject all three.

This is the editorial gate: no approval means no ThumbCanvas link and no Google Sheets write.

## 4. Create the handoff and audit it

After approval, **Resolve Human Approval** encodes only the chosen production prompt and 16:9 aspect ratio into a ThumbCanvas create URL. Opening that URL is a separate human action and may use the reviewer's ThumbCanvas plan or credits.

**Map Approved Brief to Audit Columns** creates a predictable row shape. Google Sheets auto-maps those fields to matching headers. A final check separates successful writes from credential or destination failures.

If the sheet write fails, the workflow keeps the approved ThumbCanvas link visible but clearly labels the audit failure. Fix the Sheets setup and rerun; do not treat an unsaved approval as fully completed.
